messages:
Maya: Pinging the arch crew — quick proposal: extract a very small orchestrator surface from the monolithic orchestrator into runtime-workers. Goal is to reduce tight coupling so runtime teams can iterate on scheduling/placement without touching coordinator. I’m thinking a minimal RPC surface with 3 calls: SubmitTask, PollState, Acknowledge. High-level thoughts?
Sam: +1 on decoupling. Two quick asks: define idempotency semantics for SubmitTask and be explicit about accepted vs queued responses. Also, how do we treat ordering? :thinking:
Jun: Agree with the 3-call approach. Suggest signatures like: SubmitTask(payload, idempotency_key) -> {task_id, status}, PollState(task_id) -> {status, last_event_offset, logs}, Acknowledge(task_id) -> {ack_ts}. Keep offsets so we can replay.
Priya: Ops perspective: must include trace propagation and a policy_version header so SRE can tie task latency to config changes. Also don't forget per-tenant quotas and rate-limiting signals.
Victor: One tradeoff to call out: moving logic into runtime risks duplicating retry/backoff logic. Do we centralize policy decisions or publish policies to runtimes?
Maya: Plan is coordinator remains the source of truth for policy and rollout decisions. We'll include policy_version in task metadata; runtime-workers can apply short-lived, conservative local decisions for transient failures but must re-sync with coordinator for anything older than X minutes.
Sam: Rollout idea: gateway feature-flag that routes a percentage of traffic to new runtime-workers. Need a migration path for SubmitTask schema (backwards compat). Also we should provide a shim that translates old responses for older clients.
Jun: Security note: consider signing task payloads (HMAC) so runtime can verify coordinator-issued policies. Also prefer mTLS between coordinator <> runtime.
Priya: For runbooks and SLOs: define metrics we need up front: tasks_submitted, tasks_accepted, tasks_failed, tasks_retried, tasks_stalled (>N minutes), per-policy latency histograms. Add alert thresholds and a canary escalation page.
Victor: For SDK/contract stability: use protobuf with additive fields only. Deprecation window of 6 months and a compatibility shim in the gateway. This avoids frantic rollbacks.
Maya: Good list. I'll draft an RFC that includes: API proto, auth (mTLS + optional HMAC), idempotency contract, policy_version semantics, required metrics, rollout plan, and a test harness spec. Anything crucial missing?
Jun: Test harness: we need a headless simulator to inject packet loss, delays, and policy_version skew. Also an integration test mode that runs coordinator+runtime in-process for CI.
Sam: Add a compatibility shim in the gateway so we can do staged routing even if some runtimes lag. That should be documented in the RFC as an operational requirement.
Priya: I'll own SLO definitions and the runbook (canary thresholds, manual rollback steps).
Maya: Thanks — I'll open the RFC + a small spike ticket for the simulator. tagging @here for visibility :eyes: :shipit:
deploy-bot: RFC created: https://redwood.internal/rfcs/2187654321 (draft)
Maya: Linking the draft in #engineering once I polish it. Thanks everyone for quick thoughts — will iterate on the API surface in the RFC and ping for review.
